 Few films on the 2026 calendar felt like bigger question marks than “ The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .” The prospect of Brad Pitt reprising his Oscar-winning role from “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” in a Netflix pseudo-sequel written by Quentin Tarantino but directed by David Fincher was not on many people’s bingo cards when the project was first announced. The fact that the news originally broke on April Fool’s Day even led some people to wonder if the whole thing was an elaborate joke.
 But the crowd who made their way to the TCL Chinese Theater on Monday, November 16 can attest that “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is very much real. The film was introduced by Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos, who joked that he instantly greenlit the film after receiving an 11-word text from Fincher that simply read “Written by Quentin Tarantino. Directed by David Fincher. Starring Brad Pitt.” As Sarandos tells it, he simply responded “Yes.” 
 Related Stories ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Returning to Theaters with a New Rosario Dawson Cameo — and Box Office Records and Oscar Noms in Mind 
 When the lights went down, the crowd was treated to a rollicking hangout movie filled with elaborate recreations of ’70s Los Angeles, classic rock and soul needle drops, and a meandering plot that blends crime and comedy into one elaborate excuse for Pitt’s Cliff Booth to wander around the city exuding charisma. It wasn’t long before the social media reactions began to flow in, many of which were quite positive. 
 The online buzz following the premiere praised Pitt’s willingness to do seemingly anything (a few scenes seem destined to go very viral), his romantic chemistry with Elizabeth Debicki, and the film’s unapologetic commitment to capturing both the Los Angeles of yesteryear that Booth inhabited and the style of movie that he loved to watch. And of course, there are plenty “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” Easter Eggs to go around.
 “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is set to debut for a two-week exclusive engagement in IMAX Theaters globally on November 25, 2026, before debuting on Netflix on Wednesday, December 23. Keep reading for a roundup of social media reactions following the film’s premiere.
 David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is a wild, hilarious hangout movie. Brad Pitt slides back into his beloved Oscar-winning role and gives his best performance since “Once Upon a Time in…Hollywood.” Elizabeth Debicki brings an intoxicating sensuality,… pic.twitter.com/Z4Ec0AWiAm 
— Clayton Davis (@ByClaytonDavis) November 17, 2026 
 David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of #CliffBooth pops, throbs and crackles. Like Once Upon a Time… this is a love letter to LA. An eclectic, ragtag cast make this a slick and sexy romp. A salty and slower-burning side piece to Tarantino’s original with a fire final act. pic.twitter.com/3izap5l2wp 
— Simon Thompson (@ShowbizSimon) November 17, 2026 
 THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH is my favorite movie of the year and it’s not even close. Hilarious, exciting, romantic, you’ll never guess what happens next and probably not believe it then anyway. Couldn’t love it more if I tried. pic.twitter.com/wcJmcnOJkU 
— Germain Lussier (@GermainLussier) November 17, 2026 
 THE FURTHER MISADVENTURES OF #CLIFFBOOTH is a pure riot. David Fincher’s play at a nostalgic bygone era Quentin Tarantino loves works like gangbusters. Takes time to form, but plays like a LA film noir hangout picture. Pitt & Debicki are electric together. Peter Weller, MVP. pic.twitter.com/njhxWdSm0f 
— Courtney Howard (@Lulamaybelle) November 17, 2026 
 The Further Misadventures of Cliff Booth stars charming and lethal Brad Pitt and 70s Hollywood in all its glory. But the match of brilliant and funny writer Tarantino and grim perfectionist Fincher doesn't gel. The movie is often fun to watch, but it's dark, violent, and sad.
— Anne Thompson (@akstanwyck) November 17, 2026 
 Go see The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, It’s a F—-king brilliant film. Tarantino + Fincher are perfect partners in crime to deliver this, and they do it in spades. Inject the Trent and Atticus score into my blood. Need 2 c it again pic.twitter.com/qwuMvDLKem 
— Jazz Tangcay (@jazzt) November 17, 2026
